s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic bone pain with progressive worsening and multi-system involvement
salient_findings: Diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
Intermittent generalized pruritus
Bilateral exophthalmos and blurred vision
Mild thrombocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers
Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on radiographs
Multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old man with no prior medical history
4-year history of diffuse bone pain
Bone pain worsened over the past 2 months
Developed blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
Previous workups were nondiagnostic
Treated with analgesics, vitamin D, topical steroids, and antihistamines
Normal white-cell count and differential
Normal hemoglobin
Mild thrombocytosis
Normal renal and liver function tests
Negative tumor markers and autoimmune serologies
Mildly elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on knee radiographs
Intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri on humeral radiographs
Sclerosis of the proximal ulnae and radii on forearm radiographs
Bilateral symmetric uptake on 99mTc bone scintigraphy and FDG-PET
Multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI of the lower limbs
Enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues on MRI
FDG-avid lesions on PET/CT of the brain
Bilateral perinephric soft-tissue thickening with FDG uptake on CT and PET/CT of the abdomen
CT-guided biopsy of the left proximal tibia showed diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse bone pain, bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes, and histiocytic infiltration on biopsy

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain, sclerotic changes, and histiocytic infiltration, although immunohistochemical staining does not support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Sclerosteosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes and bone pain, but lack of other characteristic features

shortlist.label: Paget's disease of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain and sclerotic changes, but absence of characteristic laboratory and radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain and sclerotic changes, but lack of characteristic laboratory and radiographic findings

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on radiographs, and multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI, along with the biopsy showing diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis, are consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease. The presence of extraskeletal involvement, such as enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: The biopsy did not show positivity for CD1a, S100, or langerin, which are typical markers for Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Sclerosteosis
rejected.why: Sclerosteosis is a rare genetic disorder that typically presents with skeletal abnormalities, but it does not typically cause the systemic symptoms or extraskeletal involvement seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Paget's disease of bone
rejected.why: Paget's disease of bone typically presents with an abnormal bone remodeling process, leading to bone enlargement and deformity, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain and symmetric sclerotic changes.

rejected.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis is a condition that typically presents with recurrent episodes of bone infection, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain and systemic symptoms.
